fact: Telecommunications Minister Boukar Michel told deputies that Starlink's concession is a multiservice Internet Service Provider licence, granted on the operator's request after a favourable ARCEP technical opinion.

The government published an order on 27 August 2025 setting conditions for Starlink's authorised operation in Chad, with user identification, 24-month log retention, and sanctions up to 12 months' suspension or withdrawal of the authorisation.
A press conference on 4 July 2025 launched Starlink in Chad, with monthly plans of 12,000 FCFA (50 GB), 18,000 FCFA (250 GB) and 32,000 FCFA (unlimited).
Chad's Ministry of Telecommunications confirmed Starlink's operating licence, approved in November 2024, with services to follow; as of this article Chad services were not yet on sale.
Starlink (SpaceX) officially obtained its operating licence in Chad, signed by ARCEP's director general and SpaceX and validated by the minister, at a ceremony on Thursday 13 March 2025.

At a 29 June 2026 debrief the telecommunications minister acknowledged Starlink's advances in Chad but regretted the limits of the packages currently offered and urged restoring unlimited offers, so Starlink service is on sale in Chad.
MyBroadband's table of Starlink status in African countries as of 17 July 2026 lists Chad as Available.
TechMag lists Chad among Starlink markets active as of mid-2026 and names it among recent launches; says Starlink is most valuable in sparsely populated areas such as Chad.

EcoMatin reports that Starlink services have been authorised in Chad for just two months, and that a ministerial arrete of 27 August 2025 sets conditions on its activity, including identifying customers with the regulator Arcep.
Dari Infos reports that in N'Djamena districts including Walia, Atrone, Chagoua and Habena residents buy one to three hours of Wi-Fi for 50 or 100 FCFA, supplied over Starlink or VSAT.
